title: Quotient-limit realization and primitive coherent-counit comparisons
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On each small pro-etale site set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathscr D_W=D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$ of whole semilinear systems, with its tensor and geometric inverse image [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized system has invertible transition adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n}:q_W^*A_m\to A_n$, where $q_W^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$, for all $m\ge n\ge1$, with the identity and quotient cocycles [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, write $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$, $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$ for $f:X\to Y$, and $U_W=(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, with the induced whole-system transitions.

Write $\mathcal R_WK=(K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n})_n$ for coherent reduction [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for total derived limit of the restricted whole system [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use the canonical adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ and its natural counit $e_A:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WA\to A$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], invertible for normalized $A$ [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Let $\widehat T_W,\widehat F_f$ be the actual quotient-complex/Roos completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

There are resolution-independent natural identifications of functors
$$r_T:\widehat T_W(K,H)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_W T_W(\mathcal R_WK,\mathcal R_WH),\qquad r_F:\widehat F_f(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_XF_f(\mathcal R_YK).$$
They use the actual quotient transitions of the defining flat-term K-flat complexes. More precisely, for a strict restricted tower $X_\bullet$ put $\mathsf C(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod X_n\to\prod X_n)[-1]$, where $s((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1})$. Countable products of module sheaves on the small pro-etale site are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. The above identifications use the natural projection-compatible isomorphism $\rho_X:\mathsf C(X)\to R\lim X$ on the derived category of strict towers [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. On a K-injective tower resolution $X\to I$, $\rho$ is $\mathsf C(X)\to\mathsf C(I)$ followed by the inverse of $\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$ with zero shifted coordinate; the representative identifications are those of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Thus these are functor comparisons, not separately chosen levelwise isomorphisms.

For normalized $A,N,C$, the maps
$$\beta_T(A,N)=\mathcal L_W(T_W(e_A,e_N))\circ r_T(\mathcal L_WA,\mathcal L_WN),\qquad\beta_F(C)=\mathcal L_X(F_f(e_C))\circ r_F(\mathcal L_YC)$$
are natural isomorphisms. After $r_T,r_F$ their inverses are the images of $T_W(e_A^{-1},e_N^{-1})$ and $F_f(e_C^{-1})$. The counits are the scalar-extension adjoints of the actual total-limit projections and satisfy $e_{A'}\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_W(u)=u e_A$ for every system map $u:A\to A'$, as an equality in $\mathscr D_W$ before evaluation. In particular the projections satisfy $p_n^{A\prime}\mathcal L_W(u)=u_n p_n^A$. This is the naturality governing these primitive comparisons, with the coefficient-extension adjunctions retained in the simultaneous system model.

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $P\to K$ and $Q\to H$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The coherent reduction functor is represented by the whole quotient complexes $P_n=P\otimes_{R_W}B_{W,n}$, not by unrelated choices at each level. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] each $P_n,Q_n$ is flat-term K-flat. These are also K-flat as whole systems: tensoring a system acyclic at every level with $(P_n)_n$ gives an acyclic complex at every level, hence an acyclic system by componentwise exactness. Thus the whole-system tensor and inverse image of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] are represented by the strict systems $Z_T=(\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes_{B_{W,n}}Q_n))_n$ and $Z_F=(f_n^*P_n)_n$. Their transition maps are exactly those in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]: the tensor transition sends $a\otimes b$ to $\tau_P(a)\otimes\tau_Q(b)$, and the pullback transition is $f^*(\tau_P)$. This is equality of the constructed strict systems, including quotient maps; it is not inferred from equality of their derived evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), with the strict Roos naturality refinement and whole-system adjunction stated by the cited nodes; agent assembly for the specified completed operations.

proof.text: Restrict $Z_T,Z_F$ to towers of $R_W$-modules or $R_X$-modules, respectively. These module categories have exact countable products by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], so [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] applies. The defining completed complexes are $\mathsf C(\operatorname{Res}Z_T)$ and $\mathsf C(\operatorname{Res}Z_F)$. Compose the representative identifications of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] with $\rho$ to obtain $r_T$ and $r_F$ on these representatives. For a K-injective tower resolution $q:Z\to I$, this is precisely $[\mathsf C(q)]$ followed by the inverse of $\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$ with zero shifted coordinate. The cited strict Roos comparison says both that this is independent of $I$ and that it preserves the actual limit projections. Its target is $R\lim\operatorname{Res}Z$, which is $\mathcal L T(\mathcal R K,\mathcal R H)$ or $\mathcal L F(\mathcal R K)$ by step 1.

proof.text: For chain maps $P\to P'$ and $Q\to Q'$ the induced maps of $Z_T$ commute strictly with the transitions: both composites send $a\otimes b$ to the tensor of the images of $\tau_P(a)$ and $\tau_Q(b)$. The same assertion for $Z_F$ is functoriality of $f^*$ applied to the transition square. Naturality of $\rho$ on the derived category of strict towers therefore gives the naturality squares for the representative comparisons. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], quasi-isomorphisms of good representatives give quasi-isomorphisms of the completed complexes, and the descended functors carry their specified natural comparisons on representatives. The whole-system functors in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and the reduction functor in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] give the corresponding comparisons on the other side. Inverting a quasi-isomorphism in each naturality square preserves the square, and composing such squares preserves it. Hence the comparisons descend to natural isomorphisms $r_T,r_F$ on all derived inputs, compatible with the representative comparisons. The unique-compatible-isomorphism clause of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] makes a change of the chosen resolution functors give the same comparisons under those specified identifications. No uniqueness assertion is based only on the projections.

proof.text: The adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] supplies one counit $e$ on the entire derived system category. Its evaluated component is the scalar-extension adjoint of the actual total-limit projection. For normalized $A$, [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] makes these canonical components isomorphisms at every $n$. Evaluation jointly detects isomorphisms by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], so $e_A$ is an isomorphism of whole systems; the same holds for $e_N,e_C$. Naturality of the counit, which is a natural transformation of whole-system functors, gives $e_{A'}\circ\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_W(u)=u\circ e_A$ in $\mathscr D_W$ for every $u$, without any normalization assumption on $u$'s endpoints. In particular this equality is available before evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), with the strict Roos naturality refinement and whole-system adjunction stated by the cited nodes; agent assembly for the specified completed operations.

proof.text: Apply the bifunctor $T_W$ to the counit isomorphisms of step 4, and then apply $\mathcal L_W$. Composing with $r_T(\mathcal L_WA,\mathcal L_WN)$ gives exactly the displayed $\beta_T$. Its inverse is $r_T(\mathcal L_WA,\mathcal L_WN)^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_W(T_W(e_A^{-1},e_N^{-1}))$: the two composites cancel by functoriality and $e_Ae_A^{-1}=1$, $e_Ne_N^{-1}=1$. Similarly the inverse of $\beta_F$ is $r_F(\mathcal L_YC)^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(F_f(e_C^{-1}))$. Thus the required inverses after the realization identifications are precisely the images of the inverse counits, with the specified directions.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), with the strict Roos naturality refinement and whole-system adjunction stated by the cited nodes; agent assembly for the specified completed operations.

proof.text: For system maps $u:A\to A'$ and $v:N\to N'$, counit naturality from step 4 and bifunctoriality give the whole-system equation $T(u,v)\circ T(e_A,e_N)=T(e_{A'},e_{N'})\circ T(\mathcal R\mathcal L(u),\mathcal R\mathcal L(v))$. Apply $\mathcal L$ and the naturality square for $r_T$ from step 3. The result is $\mathcal L T(u,v)\circ\beta_T(A,N)=\beta_T(A',N')\circ\widehat T(\mathcal L(u),\mathcal L(v))$. Applying $F_f$ to the same counit equation gives the analogous naturality square for $\beta_F$. Finally the actual total-limit projections are natural: on a tower resolution the maps are induced by the ordinary limit projections, and the projection-compatible natural $\rho$ of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] preserves their equations. Consequently $p_n^{A'}\mathcal L_W(u)=\operatorname{Res}_n(u_n)p_n^A$ (with restriction suppressed as in the statement). The evaluation description of $e$ in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] identifies their scalar-extension adjoints with $e_{A,n}$. These are the retained coefficient-extension adjunctions, rather than newly chosen evaluated comparisons.
